questions.question: Evaluate 23³ + (-15)³ + (-8)³
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the sum of three numbers **a + b + c = 0**, then the identity **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc** holds true.

Here, **a = 23**, **b = −15**, and **c = −8**.

Sum: **23 + (−15) + (−8) = 23 − 23 = 0**.

Result: **3 × 23 × (−15) × (−8) = 69 × 120 = 8280**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: **23³ + (−15)³ + (−8)³**

**Formula Used:**

**a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cbf19edb5d31e8ceb91486a99d4db415bf7e4518ccf0e8df66c7f4c51d34489.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **a = 23**, **b = −15**, **c = −8**

⇒ First, check the sum: **a + b + c = 23 + (−15) + (−8) = 0**

⇒ Substitute **(a + b + c) = 0** into the identity:

⇒ **a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (0) × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)**

⇒ **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**

⇒ **Value = 3 × 23 × (−15) × (−8)**

⇒ **Value = 3 × 23 × 120 = 69 × 120 = 8280**

**∴ The correct answer is 8280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity of Cubes

The general form is **a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)**. This is a fundamental identity used to simplify cubic expressions.

Zero Sum Condition

When the variables satisfy **a + b + c = 0**, the entire right-hand side of the identity becomes zero, leading directly to the relation **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**.

Square of a Trinomial

Another related identity is **(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)**, which is often used in conjunction with the cubic identity in competitive exams.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 180 m are moving in the same direction at speeds of 60 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. Find the time taken by the trains to cross each other.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total length** to be covered = 120 + 180 = 300 m

**Relative speed** (same direction) = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h

Convert speed to m/s ⇒ 20 × 5/18 = 50/9 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 300 ÷ (50/9) = 54 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 54 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 120 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 180 m

Speed of first train (v₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of second train (v₂) = 40 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a98cb8917ad4bd84df1b98cbd2d635f74d5254f0e82cfb34040aa9f2fff7aaea.png] 

When two objects move in the **same direction**, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds.

⇒ Total Distance (D) = L₁ + L₂

⇒ D = 120 + 180 = 300 m

⇒ Relative Speed (Vᵣₑₗ) = v₁ − v₂

⇒ Vᵣₑₗ = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18:

⇒ Vᵣₑₗ = 20 × (5/18) = 100/18 = 50/9 m/s

**Time taken (T)** = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ T = 300 ÷ (50/9)

⇒ T = (300 × 9) ÷ 50

⇒ T = 6 × 9 = 54 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 54 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two trains move toward each other, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = v₁ + v₂.

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Stationary Point Object

When a train crosses a pole or a standing man, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train itself.

questions.question: Find the value of (3+(4)/(3) of 2(1)/(4)div 2(2)/(5)-2(1)/(4) of 3(1)/(5))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression: (3 + 4/3 of 2(1/4) ÷ 2(2/5) − 2(1/4) of 3(1/5))

**Formula used:**

Follow the **BODMAS rule** (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

**Calculation:**

First, convert the **mixed fractions** into **improper fractions**:

⇒ 2(1/4) = 9/4

⇒ 2(2/5) = 12/5

⇒ 3(1/5) = 16/5

Substitute these values into the expression:

⇒ 3 + 4/3 of 9/4 ÷ 12/5 − 9/4 of 16/5

Solve the **'of'** operations:

⇒ 4/3 of 9/4 = 4/3 × 9/4 = 3

⇒ 9/4 of 16/5 = 9/4 × 16/5 = 36/5 = 7.2

The expression now becomes:

⇒ 3 + 3 ÷ 12/5 − 7.2

Next, solve the **division**:

⇒ 3 ÷ 12/5 = 3 × 5/12 = 1.25

Now, perform the **addition** and **subtraction**:

⇒ 3 + 1.25 − 7.2

⇒ 4.25 − 7.2

⇒ −2.95

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: 10 men and 15 women can complete a project in 12 days. If after 8 days, only 2/3 of the work is completed, how many more women must be added to finish the work in the next 2 days, assuming all men continue?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the daily work of 10 men and 15 women together be represented as 1 combined unit.

Total work done in 8 days = 8 units, which is 2/3 of the work. Remaining work = 1/3 of the work = 4 units.

To complete 4 units of work in 2 days, the daily requirement = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 units of work per day.

Since 10 men and 15 women provide 1 unit of work per day, we need 2 times the initial workforce to get 2 units per day.

Required workforce = 2 × (10 men + 15 women) = 20 men + 30 women. Since only men continue (10 men) and we need to find extra women, we can double the women component to reach the required work rate: 15 more women are already equivalent to the extra 10 men's share.

Let's use the standard formula: (10M + 15W) × 8 / (2/3) = (10M + 15W + xW) × 2 / (1/3)

⇒ (10M + 15W) × 4 = (10M + 15W + xW) × 2

⇒ 20M + 30W = 10M + 15W + xW

⇒ xW = 10M + 15W.

Since 10M + 15W can do 1/12 of the work per day, and 2/3 of work in 8 days matches perfectly, the addition of 10M + 15W worth of efficiency is required.

Since 10M + 15W = 25W equivalent (from work rate), the extra women needed is 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 women.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Initial group: 10 men and 15 women can complete the project in 12 days.

⇒ Work completed in 8 days = 2/3 of the total work.

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 of the total work.

⇒ Time available to finish the remaining work = 2 days.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the daily work capacity of 10 men and 15 women combined be E₁.

⇒ E₁ × 12 = Total Work (W)

⇒ In 8 days, work done = E₁ × 8 = 8/12 of W = 2/3 of W. This matches the given condition.

⇒ To complete the remaining 1/3 of W in 2 days, the required daily efficiency E₂ must satisfy:

⇒ E₂ × 2 = 1/3 × (E₁ × 12)

⇒ E₂ × 2 = 4 × E₁

⇒ E₂ = 2 × E₁

⇒ This means the new workforce must have twice the efficiency of the initial workforce.

⇒ New Workforce = 2 × (10 Men + 15 Women) = 20 Men + 30 Women

⇒ Since only 10 Men continue, the remaining capacity must be fulfilled by women.

⇒ Efficiency of 10 Men + 15 Women + x Women = 20 Men + 30 Women

⇒ 15 Women + x Women = 10 Men + 30 Women

⇒ x Women = 10 Men + 15 Women

⇒ Since 10 men and 15 women can complete 1/12 of the work daily, and from the relation of work rates we know that 10 men and 15 women can be replaced entirely by 25 women to maintain the same rate of completion under the standard efficiency ratio:

⇒ x = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 women.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence Formula

The relationship between men, women, days, and work can be generalized as (m × M + w × W) × D / Work = Constant, where M and W represent the efficiency of one man and one woman respectively.

Pipes & Cisterns Analogy

Similar to people working, pipes filling a tank use the same efficiency addition concept where Total Capacity = Sum of individual rates × Time taken.

questions.question: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume? (Use π = 22/7)

For a circle with **radius 7 cm**, the **base area** is a standard value: 154 cm².

**Volume of Cylinder** = **Base Area** × **Height**

⇒ Volume = 154 × 10 = 1540 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1540 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius (r)** of the tank = 7 cm

**Height (h)** of the tank = 10 cm

Value of **π** = 22/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8db534567b41501a812638dba0464a2cd86331fd008de0f22edd95bdc7f14ae0.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Volume (V)** of a cylinder = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 10

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 10

⇒ Volume = 154 × 10

⇒ Volume = 1540 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1540 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the side surface of the cylinder is given by the formula 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the area of the curved surface and the two circular bases is 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same **radius** and **height** as a cylinder has exactly (1/3) of its volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.

questions.question: A prize of ₹8,400 is to be shared between A and B in the ratio 3:5. Find B’s share.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio parts of **A** and **B** = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

8 units → ₹8,400

1 unit → 8400 ÷ 8 = ₹1,050

**B**'s share (5 units) = 5 × 1,050 = ₹5,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount to be shared = **₹8,400**

Ratio of **A** : **B** = **3 : 5**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01f2ba984afa2f77193cd3975a4e79f2b4fc0d8b2d07c1eeaac01055a2e099bd.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Share of a person = (Personal Ratio Part ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts) × Total Amount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 5 = 8

⇒ **B**'s share = (5 ÷ 8) × 8,400

⇒ **B**'s share = 5 × (8,400 ÷ 8)

⇒ **B**'s share = 5 × 1,050

⇒ **B**'s share = ₹5,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Distribution

If a quantity Q is divided in the ratio a:b, then the first part is [a/(a+b)] × Q and the second part is [b/(a+b)] × Q.

Inverse Ratio

The inverse ratio of a:b is 1/a : 1/b, which simplifies to b:a.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.question: Two poles of heights 10 m and 30 m stand vertically on level ground at a distance d apart. From a point on the ground between them, along the line joining their feet, the angles of elevation to their tops of the taller and the shorter poles are 60∘ and 30∘, respectively. The distance d between the poles is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base distance from **shorter pole** (10 m) for 30° = 10 × √3 = 10√3 m.

Base distance from **taller pole** (30 m) for 60° = 30 / √3 = 10√3 m.

Total distance **d** = 10√3 + 10√3 = 20√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Height** of shorter pole (H₁) = 10 m, **Height** of taller pole (H₂) = 30 m, **Angles of elevation** = 30° and 60°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81683b23de5306f914bc4f62694cbfa86b7d4bdb46a8408e992d43c27c7dc586.png] 

Let the distance from the **shorter pole** to point P be **x** and from the **taller pole** to point P be **y**.

For the **shorter pole** (Height = 10 m, θ = 30°):

⇒ tan 30° = 10 / x

⇒ 1 / √3 = 10 / x

⇒ x = 10√3 m

For the **taller pole** (Height = 30 m, θ = 60°):

⇒ tan 60° = 30 / y

⇒ √3 = 30 / y

⇒ y = 30 / √3 = (30 × √3) / 3 = 10√3 m

Total **distance** between the poles **d**:

⇒ d = x + y

⇒ d = 10√3 + 10√3

⇒ d = 20√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios for Heights

Common values used: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Pythagoras Theorem

In right-angled triangles, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 12 days, respectively. Both work for 3 days and then A leaves. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency of (**A** + **B**) = 1 + 1 = 2 units/day.

Work done in **3 days** = 2 × 3 = 6 units.

**Remaining work** = 12 − 6 = 6 units.

Time for **B** to finish = 6 units ÷ 1 unit/day = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹3,000 for 2 years at 20% per annum, interest compounded annually?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate for 2 years at 20% p.a. = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%.

Compound Interest = 44% of ₹3,000.

CI = 3,000 × 0.44 = ₹1,320.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50e9d042a9cecf43668d09957230c7479a47b6230c9729a3ac291bbe2cc5156c.png] 

⇒ A = 3,000 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 3,000 × (120 ÷ 100) × (120 ÷ 100)

⇒ A = 3,000 × 1.2 × 1.2

⇒ A = 3,000 × 1.44

⇒ A = ₹4,320

⇒ CI = 4,320 − 3,000

⇒ CI = ₹1,320

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI and SI Difference (for 2 years)

For successive growth of x% and y%, the total growth is x + y + (xy ÷ 100)%. For 2 years at rate R, it is 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

Compounding Frequencies

questions.question: If 2, x, and 18 are in continued proportion, find the positive value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When numbers **a, b, and c** are in **continued proportion**, **b** is the **mean proportional**.

Logic: **b = √(a × c)**

Applying the trick: **x = √(2 × 18) = √36 = 6**

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers **2, x, and 18** are in **continued proportion**.

**Formula Used:**

Three numbers **a, b, and c** are said to be in **continued proportion** if **a/b = b/c**, which implies **b² = ac**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eabf4fa78b5c1ba122aaec1c13725e7107b77f63bb702faa03ccccbe60040b7f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 ÷ x = x ÷ 18

⇒ x² = 2 × 18

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = √36

⇒ x = 6 (as we need the positive value)

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If **a, b, c** are in **continued proportion**, then **c** is called the **third proportional** to **a** and **b**, where **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportional

If **a:b = c:d**, then **d** is called the **fourth proportional** to **a, b, and c**, calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**.

questions.question: A spherical tank has a radius of 2 meters. If the tank is filled with water to 80% of its total volume, what is the volume of water in the tank (rounded to the nearest cubic meter)?

**Water volume** = 80% of 33.51 = 0.8 × 33.51 ≈ 26.81 m³.

Rounding to the **nearest cubic meter**, we get 27 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 m³.**

questions.question: During a sale, 50% of the goods are sold at 12% profit, 40% of the remaining goods are sold at 16% profit and the still remaining goods are sold at a loss of 19%. If there is an overall profit of x%, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of goods: **50%** (Part 1) : **20%** (40% of 50%, Part 2) : **30%** (Rest, Part 3).

Simplified ratio = **5 : 2 : 3**.

Apply **weighted average** for profit/loss: x = [(5 × 12) + (2 × 16) + (3 × −19)] ÷ (5 + 2 + 3).

x = [60 + 32 − 57] ÷ 10 = 35 ÷ 10 = **3.5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total goods = 100 units (Assumed CP = ₹100)

Part 1: **50%** of 100 = 50 units at **12% profit**

Remaining: 100 − 50 = 50 units

Part 2: **40% of remaining** = 0.40 × 50 = 20 units at **16% profit**

Part 3: **Still remaining** = 50 − 20 = 30 units at **19% loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a50de7c600b73029c08a3eee0d9fe33c3d2901c348c2f68aea5ce0a54db8baad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit from Part 1 = 50 × 12 ÷ 100 = **6**

⇒ Profit from Part 2 = 20 × 16 ÷ 100 = **3.2**

⇒ Loss from Part 3 = 30 × 19 ÷ 100 = **5.7**

⇒ **Total Net Profit** = 6 + 3.2 − 5.7 = **3.5**

⇒ **Overall Profit Percentage (x)** = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ x = (3.5 ÷ 100) × 100 = **3.5**

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Profit/Loss

When goods are divided into parts, the net profit/loss is the sum of (weight × percentage) for each part divided by the total weight. Loss is always substituted as a negative value.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the effective change is (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%. This is different from weighted averages used for parts of a whole.

Base Value Selection

Assuming a base value of 100 for calculations involving percentages simplifies arithmetic and helps avoid complex decimal fractions during competitive exams.

questions.question: Girish scored 448 marks in an examination and was 81 marks short of 46% of maximum marks. In the same examination, his friend scored 805 marks. What is the percentage of marks scored by his friend?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

46% of **Maximum Marks** = **Girish score** + 81 = 448 + 81 = 529

1% of **Maximum Marks** = 529 ÷ 46 = 11.5

Friend's **Percentage** = **Friend's Score** ÷ Value of 1%

Friend's **Percentage** = 805 ÷ 11.5 = 70%

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Girish's marks** = 448

**Difference** to 46% = 81 marks

**Friend's marks** = 805

**Formula Used:**

**Percentage of marks** = (Obtained Marks ÷ Maximum Marks) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f98861b170d160a26d714437b5180a588ee9c803c35a507da152d1e86d79364.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Maximum Marks** be 'M'.

⇒ 46% of M − 81 = 448

⇒ 0.46 × M = 448 + 81

⇒ 0.46 × M = 529

⇒ M = 529 ÷ 0.46 = 1150

⇒ Friend's **Percentage** = (805 ÷ 1150) × 100

⇒ Friend's **Percentage** = 80500 ÷ 1150 = 8050 ÷ 115

⇒ Friend's **Percentage** = 70%

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage Increase/Decrease = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Fraction to Percentage

To convert a fraction to a percentage, multiply by 100. Common values: 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 3/4 = 75%.

Base Value Concept

In problems involving percentages, the **Maximum Marks** or **Total Value** always acts as the base (100%).

questions.question: The average of 6.5, 10.8, 20 and a is 15. The value of a is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **net deviation** method relative to the average of **15**:

Total deviation must be **zero** for the 4 numbers.

Deviation of known numbers: (6.5 − 15) + (10.8 − 15) + (20 − 15) = −8.5 − 4.2 + 5 = **−7.7**

The fourth number **a** must compensate this: a = 15 + 7.7 = **22.7**

**∴ The correct answer is 22.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations = 6.5, 10.8, 20, a | Total observations = 4 | **Average** = 15

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7be9b03e39ab4447f3537e936866bc44036ebf587991b1cc6eaf643cce295b5.png] 

⇒ Sum of observations = Average × Total number of observations

⇒ 6.5 + 10.8 + 20 + a = 15 × 4

⇒ 37.3 + a = 60

⇒ a = 60 − 37.3

⇒ a = 22.7

**∴ The correct answer is 22.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The average or **Arithmetic Mean** is the central value of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the total sum by the count of items.

Net Deviation Principle

The sum of the **differences** between each number in a set and the **mean** of the set is always **zero**.

Sum Formula

To find an unknown value in a sequence when the average is known: **Sum** = Average × **Total Number of items**.

questions.question: The present age of a father is thrice that of his son. After 15 years, the age of the father will be twice that of his son. What is the present age ( in years) of the father?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present ratio of **Father** and **Son** = 3 : 1 (Difference = 2 units)

Ratio after **15 years** = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 unit)

Make the difference equal by multiplying future ratio by 2 ⇒ 4 : 2

Increase in units (4 − 3 or 2 − 1) = 1 unit → 15 years

Present age of **Father** = 3 units × 15 = 45 years

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the present age of the **Son** be x years.

Present age of the **Father** = 3x years.

After **15 years**, their ages will be (x + 15) and (3x + 15) respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c3b7ecd9adff3f648bb74ad63ed51998a97beea67614e5fc9afe11a59d05fe5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3x + 15 = 2(x + 15)

⇒ 3x + 15 = 2x + 30

⇒ 3x − 2x = 30 − 15

⇒ x = 15

⇒ **Father present age** = 3x = 3 × 15 = 45 years

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Gap

The mathematical difference between the ages of two individuals is a constant value and does not change over time.

Ratio Normalization

When solving age problems using ratios, if the time interval added is the same for both people, the difference between the ratio parts must be made equal.

Linear Equation Setup

For a person currently A years old, the age **n years ago** was (A − n) and the age **n years later** will be (A + n).

questions.question: A sum of money becomes ₹7,865 after 2 years and ₹8,651.50 after 3 years on compound interest at the same rate, compounded annually. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of interest = [(Difference in Amounts) ÷ (Amount after 2 years)] × 100

Rate (R) = [(8,651.50 − 7,865) ÷ 7,865] × 100 = (786.5 ÷ 7,865) × 100 = 10%

For R = 10%, Multiplying Factor for 2 years = (1.1)² = 1.21

Sum (P) = 7,865 ÷ 1.21 = ₹6,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** after 2 years (A₂) = ₹7,865

**Amount** after 3 years (A₃) = ₹8,651.50

**Time** gap = 1 year

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/939d306d1b37c9ca02acc2d58337afe2fbf432e6f9ed261aed67c7722270e4bc.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

The interest for the 3rd year is the **compound interest** earned on the amount at the end of the 2ⁿd year.

⇒ Interest = A₃ − A₂

⇒ Interest = 8,651.50 − 7,865 = ₹786.50

⇒ Rate (R) = (786.50 ÷ 7,865) × 100 = 10%

Now, using the formula for 2 years:

⇒ 7,865 = P(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ 7,865 = P(1.1)²

⇒ 7,865 = P × 1.21

⇒ P = 7,865 ÷ 1.21

⇒ P = 6,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Amount Property

In **compound interest**, the amount after n years becomes the **Principal** for the (n+1)th year.

Constant Ratio in CI

The ratio of amounts for equal time intervals is constant: A₂/A₁ = A₃/A₂ = (1 + R/100).

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The difference between **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** for 2 years is given by D = P(R/100)².

questions.question: If one angle of an isosceles triangle is 110°, what are the measures of the other angles of the triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle**, the angles opposite to equal sides are equal. Since **110°** is an obtuse angle, it cannot be repeated (as 110° + 110° > 180°).

Remaining sum for two equal angles = 180° − 110° = 70°

Individual base angles = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°

**∴ The correct answer is 35degree and 35degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle of an **isosceles triangle** = 110°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all internal angles of a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18e29b6938625314643e6a3121151d56101a43e8e46b70464c077bc212824bab.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the equal angles of the **isosceles triangle** be x.

In any triangle, sum of angles = 180°

⇒ 110° + x + x = 180°

⇒ 110° + 2x = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 110°

⇒ 2x = 70°

⇒ x = 70° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 35°

**∴ The correct answer is 35degree and 35degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Isosceles Triangle Property

In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite to the equal sides are equal in measure.

Obtuse Isosceles Triangle

A triangle can have only one obtuse angle (greater than 90°). In an isosceles triangle, the obtuse angle must be the vertex angle.

questions.question: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 11. If the digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original number. What is the original number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between a **two-digit number** and its **reversed** version is always 9 × (difference of its digits).

Difference of digits = 27 ÷ 9 = 3.

Sum of digits is given as 11.

Digits are (11 + 3) ÷ 2 = 7 and (11 − 3) ÷ 2 = 4.

Since the reversed number is larger, the **original number** must be the smaller one, 47.

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of digits = 11 | (Reversed Number − Original Number) = 27.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62c7862c7e652fe5d7a20c54ed5e28d5c847561439e5e26639b8d2fd6af2b650.png] 

Let the **tens digit** be x and the **units digit** be y.

⇒ Original Number = 10x + y

⇒ x + y = 11 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ Reversed Number = 10y + x

⇒ (10y + x) − (10x + y) = 27

⇒ 9y − 9x = 27 ⇒ y − x = 3 --- (Eq. 2)

⇒ Adding (Eq. 1) and (Eq. 2): 2y = 14 ⇒ y = 7

⇒ Substituting y in (Eq. 1): x + 7 = 11 ⇒ x = 4

⇒ Original Number = 10(4) + 7 = 47

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between a number and its reverse

For a two-digit number, (10x + y) − (10y + x) = 9(x − y). This means the difference is always a multiple of 9.

Sum of a number and its reverse

For a two-digit number, (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 11(x + y). This means the sum is always a multiple of 11.

General Form

Any **two-digit number** with digits a and b can be expressed in expanded form as 10a + b.

questions.question: A cyclist travels from point A to B and back from B to A along the same route. On the onward journey, he covers one-third of the distance at 12 km/hr and the remaining distance at 18 km/hr. On the return journey, he covers half of the distance at 9 km/hr and the remaining distance at 18 km/hr. Find the average speed (in km/hr) for the entire round trip.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume total distance **AB = 108 km** (LCM of 3, 2, 9, 12, 18).

Onward time (A to B) = (36 km ÷ 12 km/hr) + (72 km ÷ 18 km/hr) = 3 + 4 = **7 hours**.

Return time (B to A) = (54 km ÷ 9 km/hr) + (54 km ÷ 18 km/hr) = 6 + 3 = **9 hours**.

Total distance = 108 + 108 = **216 km** | Total time = 7 + 9 = **16 hours**.

Average Speed = 216 ÷ 16 = **13.5 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the one-way distance between **A** and **B** be **D**.

**Onward:** 1/3 D at 12 km/hr and 2/3 D at 18 km/hr.

**Return:** 1/2 D at 9 km/hr and 1/2 D at 18 km/hr.

**Formula:** **Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0cbeec2ddaa0c312634691ce0e23113fed42095283923e26d1fa7e71bc3c16f0.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = **2D**

⇒ Time for onward journey (T₁) = (D/3 ÷ 12) + (2D/3 ÷ 18) = D/36 + D/27 = (3D + 4D)/108 = **7D/108**

⇒ Time for return journey (T₂) = (D/2 ÷ 9) + (D/2 ÷ 18) = D/18 + D/36 = (2D + D)/36 = 3D/36 = **D/12**

⇒ Total Time = T₁ + T₂ = 7D/108 + D/12 = (7D + 9D)/108 = 16D/108 = **4D/27**

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (4D/27) = (2 × 27) ÷ 4 = 54 ÷ 4 = **13.5 km/hr**

**∴ The correct answer is 13.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a certain distance is covered at speed 'x' and the same distance is covered at speed 'y', then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Equal Time

If a body travels at speed 'x' for time 't' and speed 'y' for the same time 't', then Average Speed = (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price.

(A) Successive discounts of 5% and 21% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 38%, 33% and 21% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 8% discount on the first 6 toys and 27% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 3 toys free of cost on buying 7 toys.

A customer wants to buy 7 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the effective **discount percentages** for each scheme:

**Scheme A:** 5 + 21 − (5 × 21 ÷ 100) = 24.95%

**Scheme B:** Clearly much higher than 38% (first discount alone is 38%).

**Scheme C:** Average discount = [(6 × 8) + (1 × 27)] ÷ 7 = 75 ÷ 7 ≈ 10.71%

**Scheme D:** [Free items ÷ Total items] × 100 = 3 ÷ 10 × 100 = 30%

Comparing these, **Scheme C** offers the minimum discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Assume the **Marked Price (MP)** of each toy is **₹100**. For 7 toys, total **MP = ₹700**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Net Discount** = Total MP − Total SP

⇒ **Discount %** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ae921229da36f8a23d6d72ddab5dfd64f29c565b7bdbb200e3ed6c79ad768ff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Scheme A:** Net Discount % = 5 + 21 − (5 × 21)/100 = 24.95%.

⇒ **Scheme B:** This involves three successive discounts (38%, 33%, 21%). Even the first discount (38%) is greater than the others, making it highly beneficial.

⇒ **Scheme C:** Discount on first 6 toys = 6 × 8% of 100 = ₹48. Discount on 7th toy = 1 × 27% of 100 = ₹27. Total Discount = 48 + 27 = ₹75. Discount % = (75 ÷ 700) × 100 = 10.71%.

⇒ **Scheme D:** Buy 7 get 3 free implies 3 free out of 10 total toys. Discount % = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%.

⇒ Comparing all, 10.71% is the **lowest discount** value, making it the **least beneficial** to the customer.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

Successive Discount Formula

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 14, 15 and 8 leaves remainder 4 in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of the given divisors: 14, 15, and 8.

**LCM**(14, 15, 8) = 840.

The largest 4-digit multiple of 840 is 840 × 11 = 9240.

Add the required **remainder** (4) to this multiple: 9240 + 4 = 9244.

**∴ The correct answer is 9244.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 14, 15, 8

Remainder = 4

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = (Largest 4-digit multiple of **LCM**) + **Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3eea877a2886389c6451916792f42f1b38b46dcdf5b8dfe3d6e6b2882bfcb6e.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization: 14 = 2 × 7, 15 = 3 × 5, 8 = 2³.

⇒ **LCM** = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7 = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840.

⇒ Largest 4-digit number = 9999.

⇒ Dividing 9999 by 840: 9999 ÷ 840 = 11 (Quotient) and 759 (Remainder).

⇒ Largest 4-digit multiple of 840 = 9999 − 759 = 9240.

⇒ Required number = 9240 + 4 = 9244.

**∴ The correct answer is 9244.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder

When a number N is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r, the general form is N = k × LCM(a, b, c) + r, where k is an integer.

Different Remainders

If N divided by a, b, c leaves remainders r₁, r₂, r₃ such that (a−r₁) = (b−r₂) = (c−r₃) = d, then N = k × LCM(a, b, c) − d.

LCM Calculation

LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved in the given numbers.

questions.question: A school drum beats every 12 minutes, and the school bell rings every 18 minutes. If both sounded together at 9:00 AM, how many times will they sound together again before 11:00 AM?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The time interval for both to sound together is the **LCM** of their individual intervals.

**LCM(12, 18)** = **36 minutes**.

Total duration from **9:00 AM** to **11:00 AM** = 2 hours = **120 minutes**.

Number of times they sound again = **120 ÷ 36** = 3 (integer quotient).

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Frequency of **school drum** = every **12 min**

Frequency of **school bell** = every **18 min**

First simultaneous sound = **9:00 AM**

End time = **11:00 AM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28c4754278f0d37a41b83e79003d915b4d81c1f89bbc4974d09fedafc441d28d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2 × 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 18 = 2 × 3 × 3

⇒ **LCM(12, 18)** = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = **36 minutes**

⇒ The instruments sound together at intervals of 36 minutes.

⇒ Time instances: 9:00 AM + 36 min = **9:36 AM**

⇒ 9:36 AM + 36 min = **10:12 AM**

⇒ 10:12 AM + 36 min = **10:48 AM**

⇒ 10:48 AM + 36 min = **11:24 AM** (which is after 11:00 AM)

⇒ The soundings occurring **again** before 11:00 AM are at 9:36, 10:12, and 10:48.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM for Simultaneous Events

To find when multiple cyclic events occur together, find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of their time periods.

Total Occurrences Formula

Total times = (Total Duration ÷ LCM) + 1, if the starting point is included. If only **again** is asked, exclude the start.

Time Conversion

Always convert time intervals to a common unit (usually minutes or seconds) before calculating the LCM.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments to the Constitution of India introduced Fundamental Duties in the form of Article 51A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42ⁿd Amendment, 1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act**, passed in **1976** during the **Internal Emergency** (1975−1977), is the most comprehensive amendment in Indian history, often referred to as the **Mini-Constitution**.
 
• This amendment inserted **Part IV-A** and **Article 51A** into the Constitution, which originally enumerated **ten Fundamental Duties** for Indian citizens.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was incorporated based on the recommendations of the **Sardar Swaran Singh Committee**, which was constituted by the government in **1976** to suggest changes to the Constitution.
 
• These duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former **USSR** (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics) and serve as a reminder to citizens that while they enjoy rights, they also have duties toward the nation.
 
• In addition to Fundamental Duties, this amendment also added the words **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity** to the **Preamble** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **24th Amendment, 1971**

 
 
• This amendment was enacted to neutralize the effects of the **Golaknath case** judgement.
 
• It affirmed the power of the **Parliament** to amend any part of the Constitution, including **Fundamental Rights**, and made it obligatory for the **President** to give assent to Constitutional Amendment Bills.
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment, 1978**
 
 
• Introduced by the **Janata Party** government to reverse several changes made by the **42ⁿd Amendment** and provide safeguards against future misuse of emergency powers.
 
• It notably deleted the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **52ⁿd Amendment, 1985**
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, it added the **Tenth Schedule** to the Constitution.
 
• It provides for the disqualification of members of **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** on the grounds of defection from one political party to another.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes ‘disguised unemployment’ in the Indian context?

options.text: Workers are temporarily unemployed during economic slowdown.
Workers are not willing to work.
More people are employed than actually needed, with marginal productivity being zero.
Workers shift from one job to another frequently.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More people are employed than actually needed, with marginal productivity being zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disguised unemployment** is a phenomenon where the number of people working on a specific task is significantly higher than the number actually required to complete it.
 
• The defining characteristic of this state is that the **Marginal Productivity** of the extra labor is **zero**, meaning that if these surplus workers are removed, the **total production** or output will not decrease.
 
• In the **Indian context**, this is most prevalent in the **Agricultural sector**, where large families often work on small land holdings because of a lack of alternative employment opportunities in **manufacturing** or **services**.
 
• It is also referred to as **hidden unemployment** because the individuals appear to be fully employed, but their labor contribution is technically redundant to the production process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Unemployment:
 
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment**: Occurs when there is a lack of aggregate demand in the economy, typically during an **economic slowdown** or **recession**.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment**: A temporary period of unemployment that occurs when a worker is **shifting from one job to another** or searching for a new position.
 
• **Structural Unemployment**: Results from a mismatch between the **skills** possessed by the workforce and the skills required by employers, often driven by **technological advancement**.
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**: Occurs when people are unemployed at certain times of the year when demand for labor is low, such as in **agriculture** after the harvesting season or in the **tourism industry**.
 
• **Vulnerable Employment**: Refers to people working informally without proper **job contracts** or **social security** benefits, which is a major challenge in the **Indian labor market**.

questions.question: A physics lab experiment requires the measurement of temperature using the correct SI unit. Which unit should the student use to record temperature readings according to the SI system?

The correct answer is __**Kelvin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kelvin** (symbol: **K**) is the primary base unit of **thermodynamic temperature** in the **International System of Units (SI)**.
 
• Unlike the Celsius or Fahrenheit scales, the Kelvin scale is an **absolute scale**, meaning it begins at **absolute zero** (0 K), the point at which all thermal motion of particles ceases.
 
• Since 2019, the Kelvin has been defined by the fixed numerical value of the **Boltzmann constant (k)**, which is 1.380649 × 10−²³ when expressed in the unit **J K−¹**.
 
• In scientific research and **physics laboratory experiments**, Kelvin is the standard because it allows for direct proportionality in thermodynamic equations, such as the **Ideal Gas Law** (PV = nRT).
 
• The magnitude of one Kelvin is exactly equal to the magnitude of one **degree Celsius**; however, the two scales differ by an offset of **273.15** units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Celsius**

 
 
• A derived **SI unit** commonly used for everyday temperature measurements.
 
• 0 °C is defined as **273.15 K**, which is approximately the freezing point of water.
 
 
 
• **Fahrenheit**
 
 
• A non-SI temperature scale used primarily in the **United States**.
 
• The conversion formula to Celsius is °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9.
 
 
 
• **Joule**
 
 
• The **SI unit of energy**, work, or heat.
 
• It is a derived unit defined as one **Newton-meter** (1 J = 1 kg m² s−²).

• The **Charter Act of 1813** was passed by the **British Parliament** to renew the charter of the **East India Company** for another 20 years.

• While it ended the general trade monopoly, the Company was still allowed to retain its monopoly over the **trade in tea** and the **trade with China**.

questions.question: Which of the following substances should be added to acidic soil to neutralize it effectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quicklime (calcium oxide)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soil acidity** is characterized by a low pH value (below 7.0), resulting from an excess of **hydrogen ions (H+)** and a deficiency of basic cations like **calcium** and **magnesium**.
 
• **Quicklime**, scientifically known as **calcium oxide (CaO)**, is an **alkaline substance** frequently used in agriculture to raise the pH level of acidic soils to a range suitable for crop production, typically between 6.0 and 7.0.
 
• When **Quicklime** is applied to the soil, it reacts with water in a process called **slaking** (CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂), forming **calcium hydroxide**, which releases **hydroxide ions (OH−)** that neutralize the acidic **hydrogen ions**.
 
• This chemical **neutralization** helps prevent **aluminum and manganese toxicity**, which occurs at low pH levels and can severely stunt root development and overall plant growth.
 
• The use of **Quicklime** is considered more effective for rapid correction of soil acidity compared to **agricultural limestone (calcium carbonate)** due to its higher solubility and faster reaction rate in the soil profile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baking soda (Sodium bicarbonate)**:

 
 
• While **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)** is basic, its use in soil is limited because it adds **sodium**, which causes **soil sodicity**, degrades soil structure, and can be toxic to most agricultural plants.
 
 
 
• **Table salt (Sodium chloride)**:
 
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** is a neutral salt and does not possess any properties to neutralize acidity. High concentrations of salt lead to **soil salinization**, causing **osmotic stress** that prevents plants from absorbing water.
 
 
 
• **Vinegar**:
 
 
• Vinegar is a dilute solution of **acetic acid (CH₃COOH)**. Adding an acid to already acidic soil would further lower the pH, increasing acidity and potentially damaging **beneficial soil microorganisms** and plant tissues.

questions.question: What was proven to exist in an atom, by Rutherford's gold foil experiment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1911**, **Ernest Rutherford** conducted the **Alpha-ray scattering experiment** by bombarding a very thin **gold foil** with high-energy **alpha particles** (doubly charged helium ions).
 
• The experiment revealed that while most alpha particles passed through the foil without deflection, a small fraction was diverted at large angles, and approximately 1 in 12,000 particles bounced back nearly **180 degrees**.
 
• Rutherford concluded that the **positive charge** and nearly all the **mass** of an atom are not uniformly distributed but are concentrated in an extremely small, dense region at the center.
 
• This central core was named the **nucleus**, proving that atoms consist of a tiny, massive, and positively charged center surrounded by mostly **empty space**.
 
• This discovery successfully refuted the **Thomson Plum Pudding Model**, which suggested that positive charge was spread evenly throughout the atom like a pudding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electron**:

 
 
• Discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** using the **Cathode Ray Tube** experiment.
 
• These are negatively charged subatomic particles that reside in the space surrounding the **nucleus** in specific **energy levels** or orbits.
 
 
 
• **Proton**:
 
 
• While the concept of a positive charge was established by Rutherford in 1911, he specifically identified the **hydrogen nucleus** as a fundamental particle called the **proton** in **1919** through nitrogen bombardment experiments.
 
• Protons carry a positive charge equal in magnitude to the negative charge of an electron.
 
 
 
• **Neutron**:
 
 
• Discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**.
 
• These are electrically **neutral** particles located inside the **nucleus** alongside protons, accounting for the remaining mass of the atom that protons alone could not explain.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford Atomic Model**:
 
 
• Proposed that **electrons** revolve around the **nucleus** in circular paths called **orbits**, similar to how planets revolve around the sun in the solar system.

questions.question: Which of the following devices can act as both an input as well as an output device?

__
 
• A **Touchscreen** is a unique peripheral that combines the capabilities of an **input device** and an **output device** within a single physical unit.
 
• It functions as an **input device** by utilizing a touch-sensitive overlay that detects the pressure or electrical conductivity of a finger or **stylus**, converting these physical interactions into digital signals for the processor.
 
• Simultaneously, it serves as an **output device** by using an integrated **LCD (Liquid Crystal Display)** or **OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode)** panel to display visual information and feedback to the user.
 
• Common technologies used in these devices include **Capacitive** sensing (relying on electrical charges) and **Resistive** sensing (relying on physical pressure), both of which allow for direct interaction with a **Graphical User Interface (GUI)**.
 
• Because it both receives data from the user and provides data back to the user on the same interface, it is classified as a **dual-purpose** or **hybrid peripheral**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Barcode Reader**:

 
 
• This is a dedicated **input device** that uses a **laser beam** or an **image sensor** to scan and decode the printed bars of a barcode.
 
• It transmits the decoded numerical or alphanumeric data into a computer system for processing, but it cannot display information to the user.
 
 
 
• **Plotter**:
 
 
• A **Plotter** is a specialized **output device** used for printing **vector graphics**.
 
• Unlike standard printers, it uses **automated pens** to draw continuous, high-precision lines on large sheets of paper, making it essential for **Computer-Aided Design (CAD)**, engineering blueprints, and architectural plans.
 
 
 
• **Digital Camera**:
 
 
• In a computing context, a digital camera is primarily viewed as an **input device** because it captures light through a lens and converts it into digital data via **CCD (Charge-Coupled Device)** or **CMOS sensors**.
 
• This data is then transferred into a computer or storage medium for later viewing or editing.

• Under **Section 7B(2)** of the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, an OCI cardholder is specifically denied **political rights**, meaning they cannot exercise the **Right to Vote** in any **General Election** or **State Assembly Election**.
 
• OCI cardholders are ineligible to hold **public office** or **constitutional posts**, including the offices of the **President**, **Vice-President**, or **Governor** of a state.
 
• They are also barred from being appointed as **Judges of the Supreme Court** or **High Courts** and cannot be members of the **House of the People (Lok Sabha)** or the **Council of States (Rajya Sabha)**.
 
• Employment in **government services** or public sector undertakings is restricted unless the **Central Government** issues a specific notification allowing such appointments for a particular field.

• **Education and Taxation**:

• Regarding **taxation**, OCI cardholders are liable to **pay taxes** on any income earned or generated within the geographical boundaries of **India**.

questions.question: Which of the following international agreements aims to phase out ozone-depleting substances?

• The **Montreal Protocol** on Substances that Deplete the **Ozone Layer** is a global agreement finalized in **1987** and entered into force on **January 1, 1989**.
 
• It was designed to protect the **stratospheric ozone layer** by phasing out the production and consumption of **Ozone-Depleting Substances (ODS)**, which allow harmful **ultraviolet (UV-B) radiation** to reach the Earth.
 
• The treaty targets several groups of halogenated hydrocarbons, including **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, **Halons**, **Carbon tetrachloride**, and **Methyl chloroform**.

• **Paris Agreement**:

questions.question: India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) to boost global trade participation. In which year did India join the WTO?

The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India is a **founding member** of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, having joined the organization on the very day of its inception, **January 1, 1995**.
 
• The WTO was established as the successor to the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**, which had been in place since **1948**; India was also a founding member of GATT.
 
• The transition from GATT to the WTO was formalized through the **Marrakesh Agreement**, signed in **April 1994** in Morocco, following the conclusion of the **Uruguay Round** of trade negotiations.
 
• By becoming a member, India committed to a rule-based **multilateral trading system** designed to ensure transparency, predictability, and the reduction of trade barriers like **tariffs** and **quotas**.
 
• Membership allows India to invoke the **Dispute Settlement Mechanism** of the WTO to protect its commercial interests against unfair trade practices by other nations.

questions.question: The Harappan Civilization flourished mainly during which of the following archaeological eras?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bronze Age**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harappan Civilization**, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, is classified as a **Bronze Age** culture because its inhabitants mastered the art of metallurgy, specifically the production of **bronze**.
 
• Technologically, the Harappans created **bronze** by alloying **copper**, which they primarily sourced from the **Khetri mines** in **Rajasthan**, with **tin**, which was largely imported from regions like **Afghanistan** and **Hazaribagh**.
 
• Archaeological evidence from major urban centers such as **Mohenjo-daro** and **Harappa** reveals advanced bronze artifacts, including the famous **Dancing Girl** figurine, manufactured using the sophisticated **lost-wax casting** (cire perdue) technique.
 
• The civilization reached its **Mature Phase** between approximately **2600 BCE and 1900 BCE**, characterized by planned cities, drainage systems, and the widespread use of bronze for crafting tools, weapons, and ornaments.
 
• While the civilization used stone tools, the dominance of bronze for specialized craftsmanship and trade distinguishes it from the preceding stone-based eras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neolithic Age**

 
 
• This era represents the **New Stone Age**, marked by the transition from hunting-gathering to **agriculture** and **animal husbandry**.
 
• The site of **Mehrgarh** in present-day **Pakistan** is a significant precursor, showing early farming practices that eventually evolved into the urban Harappan stage.
 
 
 
• **Chalcolithic Age**
 
 
• Known as the **Copper-Stone Age**, this period involved the use of both **stone tools** and **copper**.
 
• Various regional cultures like the **Ahar-Banas** and **Kayatha** flourished in India, often overlapping with or succeeding the Harappan timeline in different geographies.
 
 
 
• **Iron Age**
 
 
• The **Iron Age** in the Indian subcontinent began long after the decline of the Harappan Civilization, starting roughly around **1000 BCE**.
 
• The **Indus people** had no knowledge of **iron**; the metal only became prominent during the **Later Vedic Period** and the era of the **Mahajanapadas**.

questions.question: The Terai belt is best described as:

options.text: A dry zone made of calcareous deposits

__
 
• The **Terai** is a lowland belt located south of the **outer foothills** of the **Himalayas** and the **Bhabar** region, spanning across parts of **India** and **Nepal**.
 
• It is characterized by a **high water table** because the streams and rivers that disappear into the **porous** rocks of the **Bhabar** zone re-emerge at the surface in this region.
 
• The re-emergence of these underground water sources creates a **damp**, **swampy**, and **marshy tract** that is naturally conducive to the growth of **thick forests** and tall grasslands.
 
• This region is historically known for its **immense biodiversity** and rich wildlife; however, over the years, significant portions have been cleared for **agriculture** to support settlement and crop production like **sugarcane**, **rice**, and **wheat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Northern Plains** of India are divided into four distinct physiological regions based on relief features:

 
 
• **Bhabar**: A narrow belt of about **8 to 16 km** in width lying parallel to the **Shiwalik** slopes, consisting of **pebbles** where rivers disappear.
 
• **Bhangar**: The largest part of the northern plain formed of **older alluvium**; it lies above the floodplains and contains **calcareous deposits** known as **Kankar**.
 
• **Khadar**: The **newer, younger alluvium** of the floodplains which is renewed almost every year, making the land highly **fertile** and ideal for **intensive agriculture**.
